blocks.title: Extension entry & session lifecycle
blocks.description: package.json registers src/index.ts as the OMP extension. The default export wires one PlannerSession per OMP session (document store, request journal, navigation state persisted in the extension's session-metadata namespace), registers the /diagram command and the visual_planner_read / visual_planner_propose tools, and follows session_start/branch/tree/switch/shutdown. It also binds the session's judge-backed related-context ranker, OMP's LSP client and $EDITOR into both surfaces.

blocks.title: /diagram command router
blocks.description: Parses `web`, `web stop`, `help`, `new [purpose]`, `open <path>`, `draft [brainstorm|plan]`, `discover [path]` and `change [goal]`; everything except web needs an interactive TUI and ends in runScreen with an optional ScreenStart.

blocks.title: Request submission
blocks.description: submitRequest registers one request and hands its prompt to the agent; submitBatch registers a batch, writes each member's instructions where its subagent reads them, and hands the parent prompt over. Shared by the overlay and web mode.

blocks.title: visual_planner_read tool
blocks.description: Resolves a block/diagram/project scope (default: the diagram on top of the navigation stack) and lists the document id, revision, dirty flag and each block's id, title, evidence and uses.

blocks.title: visual_planner_propose tool
blocks.description: Stages a proposal via ActionRegistry.stage with the branch token, document id, live document and current on-disk digest; on success fingerprints the replacement's citations (stampReplacement), persists, notifies listeners and tells the model the proposal is NOT applied.

blocks.title: Session state & branch tracking
blocks.description: SESSIONS map keyed by OMP session id; a request's branch token is `<session>:<leafId>`. adoptSession reloads branch metadata and the project file on session events so requests owned by another branch position are invalidated, not inherited; session_shutdown stops the web server and drops the session.

blocks.title: Document model & schema
blocks.description: Durable nested-diagram contract (schema version 1): DiagramDocument → root Diagram → Blocks (with optional children Diagram) and labelled Edges between siblings, plus purposes, statuses, evidence, venues, surfaces and intents. Pure functions for construction, traversal, mutation, reuse links, validation and legacy import.

blocks.title: Types & enumerations
blocks.description: Block (title, description, expectedOutput, acceptanceCriteria, position, sources with sha256 digest, evidence, status, venue, surface, mockup ≤40 000 chars, uses, actions, children), Edge, Diagram, DiagramDocument (optional git baseline), Scope and the Intent union.

blocks.title: ArkType schemas & tool parameters
blocks.description: Recursive schemas built from the host-injected arktype builder and cached per namespace; toolSchemasFor yields the read/propose tool parameter schemas.

blocks.title: Construction, traversal & mutation
blocks.description: createBlock/Edge/Diagram/Document; eachDiagram/eachBlock/findBlockLocation/findDiagramPath/findOwnedDiagram; removeBlock (drops incident edges and uses), addBlock, moveBlockInOrder, addEdge; spatial nearestBlock, cycleBlock and `path:10-40` source-ref parsing.

blocks.title: Reuse links & extract
blocks.description: addUse/removeUse, usersOutside (links a deletion would cut), extractTargets, and extractBlock: lift a block with its subtree to a containing level, the old parent now uses it and every former sibling edge becomes a use.

blocks.title: Validation
blocks.description: validateDocument: version check first, structural parse, then graph checks — id ledger, per-block and per-diagram checks, and uses refusal (self, ancestor, descendant, unknown, duplicate); validateBlock/validateDiagram for scoped replacements; missing status defaults to open.

blocks.title: Legacy board import
blocks.description: Converts ratatui-era `{ boxes, edges }` boards into one diagram: first text line is the title, the rest the description; endpoint indexes validated.

blocks.title: Document store
blocks.description: The only writer of project documents. Keeps the last on-disk digest so an outside edit is refused rather than overwritten, and holds the in-memory undo/redo history.

blocks.title: Project paths
blocks.description: `.omp-visual-planner/architecture.json` by default, `discovery/<target>` drafts, `changes/<slug>` plans suffixed -2, -3… so they never overwrite; the discover-. codebase map; the session-metadata namespace and the 2 MiB viewer cap.

blocks.title: Canonical serialization & digest
blocks.description: normalizeDocument fixes field order so structurally equal documents serialize byte-identically; digestOfText is sha256 over the text.

blocks.title: DocumentStore
blocks.description: open() (legacy boards import without a save path), transact() validates a cloned draft and bumps revision once, undo/redo (200 deep), atomic saveAs via temp file + rename with conflict refusal on digest mismatch, onSave listeners, currentDiskDigest.

blocks.title: applyReplacement
blocks.description: Applies a validated document, block or diagram replacement in one transaction while preserving identity: the document keeps its id and a scoped replacement keeps the id it replaces.

blocks.title: Request & proposal journal
blocks.description: Request/proposal lifecycle: a request token is the only way a model influences the document — one pending request, one branch, one base revision and on-disk digest. Journal states pending → submitted/staged → accepted/rejected/discarded/failed/stale; accepting is a UI action, never a tool call.

blocks.title: ActionRegistry
blocks.description: Per-session journal (last 50): begin/beginBatch refuse while a request is active; adoptBranch marks other-branch requests stale; rebase follows the planner's own saves; stage checks token, branch, state, document id, disk digest, summary, replacement shape, retention and the projected whole document; checkApplicable refuses a project proposal after any revision bump.

blocks.title: Replacement validation & retention
blocks.description: validateReplacement checks shape and ownership against the request's scope; retentionErrors refuses a replan/prune that drops a block the human already settled.

blocks.title: Shared block flow
blocks.description: Pure (no pi-tui) flow shared by the terminal screen, web mode and the composer: which verbs a purpose offers, status names, how the outline is walked, the next step, and how requests, batches and execute dispatch are composed.

blocks.title: Verbs & status cycle
blocks.description: Refine/Break down/Replan/Execute plus Sync (drift views) and Ask (file viewers); line requests add a block citing selected lines; per-purpose status cycle, labels and glyphs.

blocks.title: Outline & focus walk
blocks.description: Depth-first outline rows with collapse; focusNeighborhood (parent, inputs, outputs, children, uses links) and spatial cursor movement for the walk.

blocks.title: Next step, uses picker & sketch
blocks.description: useCandidates, extractedMessage, nextOpenBlock, progressLabel, and nextStep — the one next action per block, including Sketch when a surface lacks a wireframe fence.

blocks.title: Screens board, page fields & project actions
blocks.description: screenBoard lists pages and components with navigation and usage; pageFields/fieldLabel per purpose; project actions replan, prune and change.

blocks.title: Document starts & request composition
blocks.description: startDocument (draft/discover/change), composeRequest builds the prompt and the BeginInput registry entry, codeRootFor, changeContext (map + marked starting points), composeBatch with per-member instruction files under the OS temp dir.

blocks.title: Execute dispatch planning
blocks.description: planDispatch runs only settled plan leaves with acceptance criteria; a parent is a container; a leaf waits for its own and its ancestors' uses and inbound open edges; renderDispatch writes the task text grouped by venue.

blocks.title: Prompt composer
blocks.description: Deterministic scope prompts: resolves a scope, then writes the exact payload with authored and retrieved content delimited as data.

blocks.title: Scope resolution
blocks.description: resolveScope maps a block/diagram/project scope to its block locations, edges within it and the boundary relationships that leave it.

blocks.title: Protocol & rule sections
blocks.description: Proposal and batch output protocols, evidence rules, where-to-look limits, reuse rules and outside-block catalog (≤150), surface/sketch/build rules with DESIGN.md, related context (p ≥ 0.7, ≤ 8), drift and change-plan sections.

blocks.title: Briefs & composePrompt
blocks.description: briefFor words the task per intent, purpose and scope (replan/prune restate that settled blocks stay); composePrompt assembles it; composeBatchPrompt asks the parent to spawn one subagent per member and relay each answer.

blocks.title: Judged related context
blocks.description: Before a narrower-than-project, non-execute request, asks the session's System One judge one yes/no question per outside block and carries the likely ones into the prompt.

blocks.title: Judge role resolver
blocks.description: Resolves the `judge` model role to a judgment-API model (Jev/Laya); refuses a chat model; builds a TypeSafeJudge with an 8 s per-attempt timeout.

blocks.title: Relevance ranker
blocks.description: Candidates outside the scope (≤160) chunked 40 questions per request, ranked with a 10 s bound; one failed batch fails the ranking; summaries for single and batch previews.

blocks.title: Citation drift
blocks.description: Compares each citation's stored fingerprint with the code now, reports fresh/moved/changed/missing/unstamped/unchecked plus uncited files changed since the git baseline, and resolves them.

blocks.title: Fingerprinting
blocks.description: linesDigest (sha256, trailing whitespace ignored), refKey, stampSources/stampMissing, stampReplacement (overwrites whatever a model supplied), carryDigests across accepted proposals.

blocks.title: Drift check
blocks.description: git HEAD, per-citation state including relocation search (bounded work), uncovered changed/untracked files (≤200), checkDrift report.

blocks.title: Re-anchor, Sync & baseline
blocks.description: driftedBlockIds, syncTargets (outermost drifted blocks), syncContext for Sync prompts, reanchorMoved, prepareBaseline, changedCheck for 'still true'.

blocks.title: Terminal overlay
blocks.description: The TUI surface: one fullscreen overlay that renders its own lists, confirmations and review screens and mounts pi-tui's native Editor for text fields.

blocks.title: DiagramScreen
blocks.description: The overlay component (outline, block page, walk, map, source view, modals for edit/list/text/review/confirm/close, single and batch previews); returns closed, submit or submit-batch to the entry point.

blocks.title: Layout, routing & review diff
blocks.description: Card geometry, placeNewBlock/insertLineBlock, grid tidy and layoutNewBlocks, acceptReplacement (how every surface applies a reviewed proposal), bounded orthogonal edge routing, diffDocuments/diffIsEmpty for review.

blocks.title: Canvas & panel chrome
blocks.description: Styled cell Grid, panel chrome mirroring pi-tui's overlay-box with the host theme, and numbered syntax-highlighted source lines.

blocks.title: Web mode
blocks.description: On-demand loopback server bound to the session's own store and journal, so the browser, the overlay and a model's proposal see one document; nothing applies a proposal without a human Accept.

blocks.title: Loopback server & access control
blocks.description: 127.0.0.1 only; per-server token exchanged for an HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, Host check against DNS rebinding, Origin check on writes, strict CSP; routes /api/state, /api/files, /api/file, /api/insight, /api/outline, /api/symbol, /api/op; process-wide registry survives plugin reloads.

blocks.title: State projection
blocks.description: stateOf projects the session into WebState: focus, flow labels from flow.ts, review diff for a staged proposal, drift summary, breadcrumb.

blocks.title: Op dispatcher
blocks.description: applyOp: every op is one validated store transaction or navigation change, unknown ops/fields refused by name; composePreview ranks related context; unsaved edits answer 409 unless saveFirst; submitStart and batch requests.

blocks.title: Browser page
blocks.description: web-page.html is a self-contained Svelte bundle: scripts/build-web.ts compiles web/ into one HTML file, served verbatim by web-page.ts (WEB_PAGE). No session data is interpolated; the page polls GET /api/state (?since=version) and writes via POST /api/op; labels, verbs and statuses come from state.flow; OpenCode DESIGN.md tokens.

blocks.title: Workspace file access
blocks.description: Read-only workspace access: paths resolved and real-pathed so neither `..` nor a symlink escapes; listing via `git ls-files` (gitignore applies) or a bounded walk skipping dependency/build dirs; 5000-file and 5000-line caps.

blocks.title: Code viewer insight
blocks.description: What the file viewers can say about code: token-class highlighting, Tree-sitter syntax ranges, and on-demand language-server lookups.

blocks.title: Syntax highlighting spans
blocks.description: Runs the native highlighter with one marker color per token class and reads the ANSI back as [class, text] spans, so file text never becomes markup.

blocks.title: Tree-sitter source insight
blocks.description: inspectSource: outermost syntax block starting on a cited line plus the enclosing node chain (≤8); explicitly syntax-only, never starts a language server.

blocks.title: LSP code intel
blocks.description: Outline and symbol facts (hover, definition, references ≤100) through OMP's LSP client, loaded dynamically so a missing internal module only fails the lookup; 20 s timeout.

blocks.title: current implementation shows textual and not readable representation of symbols and other intel
blocks.description:
Both file viewers print language-server and Tree-sitter intel as raw one-line strings.

- Outline: every row is `indent + kind + name + "  :" + line` (web-page.html:1401, ui.ts:2459). Nesting is only leading spaces, the LSP kind word ("function", "property"…) takes as much room as the name, and the line number is glued to the end.
- Hover: `extractHoverText` output (code-intel.ts:224) is dumped verbatim, as a `<pre>` cut to 12 lines in the browser (web-page.html:1406) and as 8 indented lines in the terminal (ui.ts:2397-2398). Markdown fences, `---` rules and emphasis markers show up literally, and the signature is not highlighted.
- Definitions/references: a flat list of `path:line  preview` buttons (web-page.html:1398, 1407-1408) or →/← rows (ui.ts:2401). No grouping by file, no per-file counts, and the preview line is plain text.
- Syntax insight in the terminal is a status message of raw grammar kinds, `syntax: function_declaration › statement_block · block a–b` (ui.ts:2348-2349).

The data is already there: `OutlineSymbol` has name/kind/depth/lines, and `SymbolFacts` has hover/definitions/references/truncated (code-intel.ts:30-50). This block is about presentation only.
blocks.expectedOutput: The outline, symbol (hover/definition/references) and syntax-insight views in the browser and the terminal show intel a person can scan: structured, highlighted and grouped. Formatting comes from one shared pure helper, so the two surfaces show the same labels. The `/api/outline` and `/api/symbol` payloads and the LSP lookups are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Hover renders its markdown: fenced code appears as syntax-highlighted code (highlightLines in the browser, the native highlighter in the terminal), prose wraps as text, and `---` becomes a separator; no literal ``` or `---` is visible for a TypeScript hover from the TS server.

Outline rows show a short kind label (e.g. fn, class, method, prop, var) visually distinct from the emphasized symbol name, with the line number dimmed and right-aligned; children are drawn as a tree under their parent, not just as extra spaces.

Definitions and references are grouped by file, with a per-file count and the currently open file first; each row shows its line number and a syntax-highlighted preview; `truncated` still shows as a `+` on the total.
Terminal syntax insight humanizes node kinds (`function_declaration` → `function declaration`) and says which block range it covers, and still states it is syntax only.
File text and server text never become markup: the browser builds nodes with textContent/token spans only, and the terminal strips terminal escape sequences from server text before rendering.

Unit tests cover the shared formatter: a hover with a fenced signature plus prose, a nested outline with mixed kinds, and references across two files with truncation; `bun test` and `bun run check` pass.

blocks.title: External block editing
blocks.description: Edit one block as markdown in the user's own editor.

blocks.title: Block ↔ markdown codec
blocks.description: `# Title`, free-markdown body, then one `## <field>` section per structured field the purpose uses; only a known-field `##` ends the body and fenced code stays text; a deleted section clears its field.

blocks.title: $VISUAL/$EDITOR launcher
blocks.description: Writes a temp .md, runs `sh -c '<cmd> "$1"'` with the terminal inherited, returns the saved text or null on non-zero exit, always removes the file.

blocks.title: Decompose skill
blocks.description: Markdown fallback when no planner document is open: one PLAN.md of nested two-space bullets (Logseq-style) with note/status/venue/id fields, one node per turn, /tree as history; defers to the visual_planner tools when available.

blocks.title: Demo recording tooling
blocks.description: fixture.ts writes a disposable explore workspace (copies of src/flow.ts and src/actions.ts plus a small cited document); scenario_full.py drives real `omp -e src/index.ts` in a pty and records a model-free tour to an asciicast.

blocks.title: Test suite
blocks.description: `bun test` over test/*.test.ts, one file per module (model, store, actions, compose, flow, dispatch, drift, relevance, judge, ui, screen, web, highlight, code-evidence, code-intel, block-markdown); `tsc --noEmit` is the check script.
